_about: Water (1) + ethyl acetate (2): heterogeneous (two-liquid) azeotrope at 101.325 kPa, as tabulated in the Wikipedia 'Azeotrope tables' article. Row as printed: azeotrope boiling point in degC and composition in weight percent of ethyl acetate (the second component).

source.citation: Azeotrope tables, Wikipedia, table 'binary azeotropes of water', row ethyl acetate; values from Lange's Handbook of Chemistry (10th ed., 1961) and the CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics (44th ed., 1962)
source.access: Open (CC BY-SA text; handbook values). Secondary compilation, the same source as validation/data/azeotropes_101kPa.json.
source.tables: Binary azeotropes of water, row 'ethyl acetate': b.p. of mixture 70.4 degC, % by weight 91.9 (U 96.7, L 8.7)

notes: Old handbook values (1961/1962), no uncertainty given. 91.9 wt % ethyl acetate is the overall (vapour) azeotrope composition; the layers are 96.7 wt % ethyl acetate (upper, U) and 8.7 wt % (lower, L), at an unstated temperature, not used. validation/python/fit_parameters.py converts 91.9 wt % to the vapour mole fraction of water with the molar masses in src/data/components.json (y_water = 0.301). Used as a weighted fit target for water + ethyl acetate because no open finite-concentration VLE data for this pair was found. Read twice from the Wikipedia page, both reads identical.
